The *Yuganaddhakathā* ("Discussion of Coupling") is a chapter of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 2.1) preserved in the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text is closely related to the *Yuganaddhasutta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 4.170) and its Chinese counterpart SA 560 [SuttaCentral]. Four modern translations in four languages are cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary literature passages gathered in this dossier directly examine this specific *Paṭisambhidāmagga* treatise, referring instead to the discourse in AN 4.170 or to the homonymous technical concept of *yuganaddha* ("union" or "two-in-one") in late Indian and Tibetan Tantric traditions.
Text-reuse analysis reflects extensive reuse across canonical and post-canonical Pali literature, with DharmaNexus recording 3,434 matching segments shared with 107 texts [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral's identification of the text's connection to AN 4.170 is confirmed by DharmaNexus, which detects a 0.95 similarity match across segments §0.3–8.0 of Ps 2.1 and §170.0.2–170.7.1 of the Catukkanipāta [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Substantial shared material also occurs within the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* itself—notably with the *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1; 294 matches) and the *Ānāpānassatikathā* (Ps 1.3; 168 matches)—as well as with the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* (244 matches) and Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga* (156 matches, showing up to 0.84 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. Further canonical reuse appears with AN 5, AN 9, MN 20, and the Yamaka [DharmaNexus].
Cross-language computational alignments link segments of the *Yuganaddhakathā* with several Tibetan canonical translations and Sanskrit treatises, including the *Śatasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitābṛhaṭṭīkā* (D3807), the *Arthaviniścayaṭīkā* (D4365), the *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra*, the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra*, Vasubandhu's *Madhyāntavibhāgabhāṣya*, Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*, and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* [DharmaNexus].
